title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a typescript sheet photographed upside down. It is unrelated to the surrounding handwritten notes on Frobenius, tori and motives. In content and numbering it matches SGA 4, Exposé VIII ('Foncteurs fibres, supports, étude cohomologique des morphismes finis'), Remarque 3.13, and is presumably a stray sheet of that exposé's typescript filed in this folder.

Context: 3.5 b) says that the fibre functors F ↦ F_{x̄} at geometric points x̄ of X, for x running over all points of X, form a conservative family on the étale topos X_et. Corollaries 3.6–3.8 deduce consequences: testing monomorphisms, epimorphisms, isomorphisms and exactness on stalks.

The remark generalises this. Let E ⊂ X be a set of points such that for every étale X' → X the preimage E' is 'très dense' in X' (EGA IV 10.1.3): every open of X' containing E' is all of X'. Then the stalk functors at geometric points over x ∈ E already form a conservative family.

Proof, as in 3.5 b). Let s, t be sections of a sheaf over an étale X' whose germs agree at all geometric points over E'. They agree on an étale neighbourhood of each such point. The images of these neighbourhoods are open, since étale maps are open, so their union is an open subset of X' containing E'. By very-density it is all of X', so s = t. Surjectivity on stalks is handled the same way.

The hypothesis holds in three cases:
- (a) X is Jacobson (EGA IV 10.4.1), e.g. locally of finite type over a field or over Z, and E is the set of closed points.
- (b) X is locally of finite type over a prescheme S, and E is the set of points closed in their fibre.
- (c) X is locally noetherian, and E is the set of x with closure {x}‾ finite, i.e. a semi-local scheme of dimension ≤ 1 (EGA IV 10.5.3, 10.5.5).

In each case the property is stable under étale base change: Jacobson-ness and the fibrewise and noetherian conditions pass to étale X'.

The remark serves étale cohomology: in practice one can check exactness and isomorphisms of étale sheaves at closed points only.
errors: No mathematical error. The proof is only sketched ('cela se voit immédiatement'), but the argument is standard and correct.
In (c), 'semi-local de dimension ≤1' should be read as: the closure {x}‾ is a finite set, hence a noetherian space of dimension ≤ 1. This is consistent with EGA IV 10.5.3.

ideas.what: Conservativity of fibre functors at geometric points lying over a 'very dense' set of points, stable under étale base change.
ideas.modern_name: Checking étale sheaf properties at closed points (stalks at a very dense set)
ideas.where_published: Appears to be SGA 4, Exp. VIII, Remarque 3.13 (LNM 270, 1972), which this text matches.

ideas.what: Examples of such sets: closed points of Jacobson schemes, points closed in their fibre for schemes locally of finite type over S, and points with finite closure in locally noetherian schemes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of SGA 4 Exp. VIII (Remarque 3.13), published and standard. It is misfiled among the 1965 motivic Galois theory notes and has no connection to them.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down (rotated 180°).
'pour x E' should read 'pour x ∈ E'; similarly 'choisir x ∈ E' and 'x ∈ X tels que'.
'qui sont fermé dans leur fibre' should read 'fermés' (typo in the original).
'Jacobson' is typed with a struck/overtyped J ('Ĵacobson'); the reading is Jacobson.
There is an overtyped '10.5.5' at the end; the reading is 'EGA IV 10.5.3. et 10.5.5.'
